sources.entry: Generate an Average Face using Python and OpenCV

summary.title: Average Face : OpenCV ( C++ / Python ) Tutorial
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build an average face by aligning faces with dlib 68-point landmarks, a similarity transform, Delaunay triangulation and triangle warping, then averaging pixel values in OpenCV (C++ and Python).
takeaways: Normalize each face to a shared 600x600 frame by aligning the outer eye corners (landmarks 36 and 45) with a similarity transform.
Use estimateAffinePartial2D with LMEDS; OpenCV needs three point pairs, so a third point is added to form an equilateral triangle.
Average pixel values only after warping each face's triangles to the mean landmark positions, using Delaunay triangulation over 68 points plus 8 boundary points.
The page also notes OpenCV 5 and NumPy changes: estimateRigidTransform and np.int are replaced, and Subdiv2D moves to the geometry module.
summary.summary: The tutorial explains the history of face averaging, from Galton's 1878 work to later findings on attractiveness, then gives a four-step method: detect 68 dlib landmarks, normalize faces with a similarity transform to eye-corner positions, align features by warping Delaunay triangles to mean landmark positions, and average the warped images. It includes C++ and Python snippets for the transform and example results on public figures. An appended compatibility update covers running the Python and C++17 code, OpenCV 5 and NumPy fixes, and production limitations such as landmark errors, consent, and outlier sensitivity.
